english.note: Use 長氣 for something drawn-out and wearisome, especially speech, explanations, or procedures.
Use this when the person is talkative in a tiresome, repetitive, or long-winded way.
Use this for speech or writing that is excessively long, repetitive, or needlessly detailed rather than simply unnecessary.
Use 長氣 for someone who talks for too long or goes on and on.

examples.english: Your explanation is so tedious that even I get tired listening to it.
examples.traditional: 你份解釋咁長氣，聽到我都攰。
examples.jyutping: nei5 fan2 gaai2 sik1 gam3 coeng4 hei3 teng1 dou3 ngo5 dou1 gui6

examples.english: My uncle gets really talkative and long-winded whenever he starts talking about that film.
examples.traditional: 阿叔一講起嗰套戲就好長氣。
examples.jyutping: aa3 suk1 jat1 gong2 hei2 go2 tou3 hei3 zau6 hou2 coeng4 hei3

examples.english: Your report is too redundant; you have said the same thing three times.
examples.traditional: 你份報告太長氣，講咗三次同一樣嘢。
examples.jyutping: nei5 fan2 bou3 gou3 taai3 coeng4 hei3 gong2 zo2 saam1 ci3 tung4 jat1 joeng6 je5

examples.english: You’re being so windy—please get to the point.
examples.traditional: 你唔使再講喇，真係好長氣。
examples.jyutping: nei5 m4 sai2 zoi3 gong2 laa3 zan1 hai6 hou2 coeng4 hei3
